texts: good. the conditional becomes a rule the reasoner can actually fire: the Keeper, the lantern, the untended state, the overnight timing and the 'before dawn' deadline are all carried, and a dying is derived for each triggering occurrence.

good. it parses to a fireable rule with the lantern, the untended state, the night and the 'before dawn' bound all present. The one nuance that does not survive is the durative 'through' — the night is recorded as when the lantern was untended, not as a whole-night span — and no rewrite recovers it, since there is no way to express a span across a part of the day.

bad: the two actions are welded into a single rule, so trimming the wick can only be derived together with refreshing the mire-essence, and the 'each' quantifier is forced to name two verbs at once; 'during the night' also has no licensed form and quietly falls back on a plain night time slot. Split the coordination into one finite clause per action and use the plain day-part wording: "Each Keeper refreshes the mire-essence at night. Each Keeper trims the wick at night."
